# 8-Bit Vinyl Player

> A pixel-art turntable in one HTML file. It plays the listener's own audio files in the browser on a deck drawn on an 84-pixel grid in the colours of an NES, a Game Boy or a C64. It keeps the deck model of the Realistic Vinyl Player it is based on (platter spin-up and coast-down, a pivoted tonearm that tracks across the whole record, pitch that follows platter speed, generated surface noise) and adds chip-style mechanical sounds and a Crush fader that reduces the music's bit depth and sample rate. No build step, nothing to install, no network requests; it works offline and from file://.

Everything is in `index.html`: inline CSS and JavaScript, organised by section comments, with all tunable constants in one block at the top of the script. The Press Start 2P font is embedded in the file (SIL Open Font License, see OFL.txt). A MilkDrop visualizer (butterchurn 2.6.7 with its minimal preset pack, MIT) is inlined unmodified in a separate script block above the player's own; the VIZ button shows it on the record label, or spectrum bars written after Musializer (MIT), a ridgeline, a scope, a spectrogram or a radial spectrum on the deck's grid. Deck settings hold a Winamp-style ten-band graphic EQ with Winamp's presets (values from Webamp, MIT) and .eqf import, and the DESK button shows the library as artist and album folders. Audio files, cover art and settings stay in the browser (IndexedDB `vinyl-db`, localStorage keys `vinyl-prefs`, `vinyl-tracks`, `vinyl-deck`, `vinyl-eq`, `vinyl-eq-presets`), shared with the Realistic Vinyl Player when both are served from the same address.

URL switches: `?demo` loads three synthesized tracks, `?selftest` runs the built-in assertions, `?debug` exposes the deck state as `window.__deck`.
